newsitem.title: INDIA: India to set insurance rules within three months.
newsitem.headline: India to set insurance rules within three months.

text.p: India plans to set rules governing private and foreign participation in its insurance sector within three months, the head of the country's insurance watchdog said on Friday.

"You have waited so long, you will not mind waiting for another two or three months when you are told you have to get set and run the race," N. Rangachari, chairman of the Insurance Regulatory Authority of India, told a global conference on insurance.

Two state-owned companies, the Life Insurance Corp (LIC) and the General Insurance Corp (GIC), have controlled the local industry since life insurance was nationalised in 1956 and general insurance in 1972.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram last month announced plans that would let only Indian firms participate in health insurance and pension schemes through joint ventures with LIC and GIC.
Rangachari indicated the government may still consider it premature to allow foreign firms into the insurance field.
"It has always been on the cards that the joint venture will be only an Indian company," he said.
"The route to privatisation would be through an Indian company which would be formed in India and subject to the rules of Indian company administration."

Communist partners within India's fractious 15-party coalition government have bitterly opposed proposals for foreign participation in the sector, which is being opened under an economic reforms programme launched in 1991.

Chidambaram last month emphasised that LIC and GIC would retain their monopoly status despite economic liberalisation. The Finance Ministry estimates the insurance sector is growing at the rate of about 11 percent annually.
